Definition: from a compound of G1223 and G1210; a "diadem" (as bound about the head):--crown. Compare G4735.
BiblicalUsage: A diadem is a crown bound about the head, the crown of a king, and Revelation sets three of them before us. The dragon wears seven, the beast wears ten, and the Rider on the white horse wears many — and the difference between them is everything.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the crowns in Revelation are the test of who truly reigns. The dragon and the beast wear borrowed glory that fades, but Christ wears many crowns because the kingdom is His by right, and His victory is the one that lasts.
RelatedTopics: Kingship of Christ; End Times; Victory
